tour.overview:
For more than 1,600 years Istanbul was the capital of two empires, first as Constantinople under the Byzantines and then as the seat of the Ottoman sultans, and almost all of that story can be walked in one square kilometre of the old city. This private day takes you through it with a licensed Istanbul guide. You enter Hagia Sophia, finished in 537 under the emperor Justinian, whose dome seemed to float above the world for a thousand years, then cross to the Blue Mosque, built by Sultan Ahmed I in the early 17th century and named for the blue Iznik tiles inside. Between them lies the Hippodrome, where chariot races once roared and an Egyptian obelisk still stands.

After descending into the Basilica Cistern, a forest of columns lit above dark water, and lunch nearby, you spend the afternoon at Topkapı Palace, from which the sultans ruled an empire across three continents. Its courtyards, pavilions and treasury look out over the meeting of the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Istanbul
• Type: private walking tour with licensed guide (and car for hotel transfers where needed)
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km of walking on old streets

WHAT YOU SEE
• Hagia Sophia (upper gallery visitor route).
• The Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque).
• The Hippodrome: the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
• The Basilica Cistern.
• Topkapı Palace and its treasury.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide orders the visits around prayer times and queues, so you see the mosques when they are open to visitors and Topkapı when the morning crowds have gone.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Istanbul, families, history lovers and anyone with only one or two days in the city.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the Bosphorus, the bazaars and the Asian side, see our Bosphorus cruise and bazaar tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
For the mosques, shoulders and knees must be covered and women need a headscarf (available at the door). Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays; on those days we replace it with the Süleymaniye Mosque or the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.

days.name: Sultanahmet: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, the Cistern and Topkapı
days.description:
What to expect: a private day on foot through Byzantine and Ottoman Istanbul, with a licensed guide, tickets and lunch.

Your guide meets you at your hotel at about 9:00. You begin at Hagia Sophia, built in just five years and finished in 537 for the emperor Justinian. For nearly a thousand years it was the largest church in the world; after 1453 it became a mosque, then a museum in 1934, and a mosque again in 2020. Visitors now follow a route through the upper galleries, which is the best place to see the great dome, the Byzantine mosaics of Christ, the Virgin and emperors, and the huge Ottoman roundels bearing the names of God, the Prophet and the first caliphs. Your guide explains how the building was used by both faiths.

Across the garden stands the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, the Blue Mosque, built between 1609 and 1616, with six minarets and more than 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles in its prayer hall. Beside it lies the Hippodrome, once the stage for chariot races and riots, where you see the Obelisk of Theodosius, carved for Pharaoh Thutmose III around 1450 BC and brought from Egypt in 390 AD, and the bronze Serpent Column from Delphi. Next you go down into the Basilica Cistern, built in the 6th century to store the city's water: 336 columns rise from the shallow water in a dim, golden light, and two upside-down Medusa heads support columns at the far end.

After lunch at a local restaurant, you spend the afternoon at Topkapı Palace, the residence of the Ottoman sultans from the 1460s until the mid-19th century. You walk through its courtyards and kitchens, the council hall where the viziers met, the treasury with the Spoonmaker's Diamond and the Topkapı dagger, and the pavilions overlooking the Bosphorus. The Harem can be added with a separate ticket. You are back at your hotel at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Meet your guide at your hotel.
09:15 – Hagia Sophia (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
10:45 – The Blue Mosque and the Hippodrome (about 1 hour).
12:00 – The Basilica Cistern (about 45 minutes).
13:00 – Lunch in Sultanahmet.
14:15 – Topkapı Palace (about 2 hours 30 minutes).
17:00 – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Blue Mosque closes to visitors for about 90 minutes at each prayer time and longer on Friday at midday; your guide plans around this.
• Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays; we replace it with the Süleymaniye Mosque or the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
• Entry to Hagia Sophia for visitors is by the upper gallery route; the ground floor is reserved for worship.

INCLUDED: licensed private guide, tickets to Hagia Sophia, the Basilica Cistern and Topkapı Palace, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: the Topkapı Harem, drinks at lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is Hagia Sophia open to visitors?
faq.answer: Yes. Since it became a mosque again, visitors buy a ticket and follow a route through the upper galleries, which give the best views of the dome and mosaics. The ground floor is for worshippers.

faq.question: Is the Blue Mosque free?
faq.answer: Yes, entry is free, but it closes to visitors at prayer times. Your guide times the visit so you can go in.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Clothes covering shoulders and knees. Women cover their hair in the mosques; scarves are available at the entrance. Shoes are removed inside.

faq.question: Is the Topkapı Harem included?
faq.answer: No, it needs a separate ticket. It is well worth it if you are interested in palace life; tell us and we will add it.

faq.question: What if we visit on a Tuesday?
faq.answer: Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays. We replace it with the Süleymaniye Mosque and its views, or the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: About 5 km over the day, on cobbled streets and palace courtyards, with breaks. The sites are close together.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the cistern, the treasury and the stories of sultans. The guide adapts the pace.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, Turkish lunch at a local restaurant in Sultanahmet. Vegetarian options are always available.

faq.question: Can we skip the queues?
faq.answer: We book tickets in advance where possible and plan the order to avoid the busiest times, but security checks are the same for everyone.

faq.question: Can we add the Grand Bazaar?
faq.answer: Yes. The Grand Bazaar is a short walk away and can replace the Cistern or be added at the end of the day.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to November are pleasant. Summer is busy and warm; winter is quieter, with some rain.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
